item.title: Selective and differential media answer different questions
item.content: Selective media contain conditions that favor or inhibit particular groups, while differential media reveal visible differences among organisms growing on the medium based on biochemical or physiological traits.
item.explanationMarkdown:
A single medium can be both selective and differential.

- **Selective** asks: *who is able or favored to grow under these conditions?*
- **Differential** asks: *how can organisms that grow be distinguished by a visible reaction?*

This distinction helps interpret culture results without confusing growth inhibition with diagnostic color or reaction changes.

cards.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes selective from differential media?
options: Selective media distinguish colony colors only; differential media kill unwanted organisms.
Selective media favor/inhibit particular groups; differential media reveal visible trait differences among organisms that grow.
Selective and differential are synonyms for nutrient-rich media.
Differential media can never also be selective.
cards.explanation: Selection changes which organisms are favored/inhibited; differentiation reveals distinguishable reactions. A medium can do both.
